sealed_candidate.answer: ## Recommended outcome and comparison for judging agent productivity (q1 / o1 = unresolved on closure, per fixture limits; decision framework is supported by policy only as a measurement policy, not by measurements — see limits below for why o1 cannot be closed as *supported* by the pilot data alone.) Use the measurement policy's declared evaluation set as the outcome, and a matched-task comparison as the baseline. Do not use accepted-PR counts as a causal productivity measure; the policy explicitly forbids inferring causal benefit from accepted-PR counts, and the pilot note supplies no comparison data.

claims.text: Agent-assisted delivery should be evaluated using matched tasks, quality gates, human review time, rework, elapsed lead time, and total cost as the declared outcome set.
claims.uncertainty: No material uncertainty: this is the explicit policy definition.

claims.text: Failed or abandoned tasks must be counted; productivity cannot be inferred causally from accepted-PR counts.
claims.uncertainty: No material uncertainty: policy-stated accounting boundary.

claims.text: The only available data point is 40 accepted pull requests in one month, with no task mix, control group, reviewer hours, failure count, or provider costs reported.
claims.uncertainty: No material uncertainty about what the pilot note contains; material uncertainty remains about actual productivity because these elements are absent.

claims.text: The 40-PR figure cannot support a conclusion that agent assistance improved productivity.
claims.uncertainty: Unresolved by design: no baseline or comparison exists in the supplied sources.
